 The Edge Singapore Tue, 3 November 2026 at 10:50 pm GMT-7 1 min read F34.SI +1.69% 
 Wilmar is one of the ten companies asked by the Singapore government to deal with the recurring trans-boundary haze 
 George Yeo, an independent director of Wilmar International, has raised his stake in the company after buying 100,000 shares at $2.97 each on Nov 4. Yeo, a retired minister, now owns just over 1 million shares. 
 Wilmar is in the news recently as one of the ten companies with operations in Indonesia, that have been asked to deal with the recurring issue of trans boundary haze. 
 He was among the few prominent local figures were named by the Straits Times as individuals with links to these companies. 
 Yeo was appointed to Wilmar's board on April 19 2024. After he left politics, Yeo held executive roles in the Kerry group of companies, which, just like Wilmar, is controlled by the Kuok family. 
 From a recent high of nearly $4 in August, Wilmar shares have dropped by around a quarter to close at $2.96 on Nov 4.
